key_insight: UniMotion introduces a single end-to-end model that jointly understands and generates human motion, natural language, and RGB images by representing motion as a continuous modality rather than discrete tokens, preserving temporal continuity and avoiding quantization artifacts.
problem_solved: Existing unified models handle only limited modality subsets (e.g., Motion–Text or Pose–Image) and rely on discrete tokenization that causes quantization error and breaks temporal coherence; UniMotion enables seamless cross-modal understanding and generation across motion, text, and images without those drawbacks.
method: Unified architecture that ingests and emits three modalities (motion, text, RGB) in a shared latent space to support both understanding (retrieval, classification) and generation (synthesis, captioning).
Continuous motion representation (trajectory-aware embeddings) replacing discrete tokenization to preserve fine-grained temporal dynamics and reduce quantization noise.
Multimodal training objectives (cross-modal alignment + conditional generation losses) to learn bidirectional mappings between motion, language, and images in one model.
impact: Provides a practical, single-model solution for applications needing coherent motion–language–vision coupling (animation, embodied AI, human–robot interaction), simplifying pipelines and improving temporal fidelity in generated motion and cross-modal retrieval.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing three modality ports (motion, text, image) converging into a shared latent model and branching to understanding/generation heads.
Timeline comparison: continuous motion trajectory (smooth curve) vs discrete tokenized frames (stair-step) to illustrate reduced quantization and preserved temporal continuity.
Example triplets: input text → synthesized motion skeleton → rendered RGB frames, side-by-side with ground truth to showcase generation quality.
Evaluation chart highlighting improvements in temporal coherence and cross-modal retrieval/conditional generation metrics (e.g., coherence score, retrieval accuracy).
paper_title: UniMotion: A Unified Framework for Motion-Text-Vision Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ziyi Wang, Xinshun Wang, Shuang Chen, Yang Cong, Mengyuan Liu
